provenance.title: Antimicrobial stewardship — the prompts that shorten, narrow and stop antibiotics
provenance.primarySource: WHO AWaRe antibiotic classification and antimicrobial stewardship in health-care facilities toolkit, 2019
provenance.why: Most antibiotic harm — resistance, C. difficile, avoidable toxicity and cost — comes not from the decision to start but from the failure to review. Stewardship is the discipline of the second look: switch intravenous to oral once the patient is improving and can swallow, narrow empirical broad-spectrum cover the moment a susceptibility result names the organism, stop or justify a course that has run past its indication, and never let a WHO AWaRe Watch or Reserve agent run without a documented indication, a stop/review date and, for Reserve, stewardship approval. These rules encode those prompts so the review happens on time rather than not at all.

sourceVerification.note: The WHO AWaRe / AMS toolkit is NOT vendored under docs/reference/who-dak/MANIFEST.json. Authored against the 2019 AWaRe classification and the antimicrobial stewardship in health-care facilities toolkit; ships ENGINEERING_SEED until the primary text is vendored. The AWaRe Access/Watch/Reserve groupings are WHO principle; the numeric day thresholds here (review at 7 days, Watch-group review at 5 days) are placeholders pending the national antimicrobial guideline and MOHCC ratification.

rules.name: On IV antibiotic, improving and tolerating oral — switch to oral
rules.message: Consider switching from intravenous to oral antibiotic — the patient is improving clinically and tolerating oral intake.
rules.explanation: Prolonged intravenous therapy adds line-related infection, thrombophlebitis and cost without benefit once a patient is improving and can absorb an oral agent. WHO stewardship prompts an IV-to-oral (IVOS) review at the point clinical improvement and oral tolerance coincide, using an oral agent with adequate bioavailability for the indication.
rules.requiredAction: Review for IV-to-oral switch: confirm the oral agent has adequate bioavailability for the site of infection, switch where appropriate, and record the switch decision.
sourceRefs: WHO AWaRe / AMS toolkit 2019 — intravenous-to-oral switch (IVOS) review

adaptation.whoStatement: Review the intravenous-to-oral switch once the patient is clinically improving and tolerating oral intake.

testCases.name: improving and tolerating oral on IV — prompt switch
not yet tolerating oral — do not prompt
not on an IV antibiotic — rule does not apply
clinical improvement never assessed — cannot conclude switch

rules.name: Antibiotic course past the review point — review necessity
rules.message: Antibiotic has continued to or beyond the review point without a documented review — review the need to continue, narrow or stop.
rules.explanation: Antibiotics continued beyond the recommended course drive resistance and toxicity without added benefit. WHO stewardship requires a scheduled review of every continuing course; a course that has reached the review threshold with no review on record should trigger an active decision to continue with justification, narrow, or stop.
rules.requiredAction: Review the course now: confirm the indication still holds, narrow or stop where possible, and if continuation is justified record the reason and a new stop/review date.
sourceRefs: WHO AWaRe / AMS toolkit 2019 — antibiotic review and duration

adaptation.whoStatement: Every continuing antibiotic course must be reviewed against its indication and recommended duration.
adaptation.nationalStatement: The review point is provisionally set at 7 days pending the national antimicrobial guideline; the principle of a scheduled review is adopted as published.
adaptation.rationale: WHO states the review principle but recommended durations are indication-specific. A single 7-day threshold is an engineering placeholder to trigger review, not a WHO-stated cut-off, and must be replaced by indication-specific durations on national ratification.
evidenceRefs: WHO AWaRe / AMS toolkit 2019 — review and duration

testCases.name: course at review point with review overdue — prompt review
course at review point but review already done — do not prompt
short course not yet at review point — rule does not apply
review status never recorded — cannot conclude overdue

rules.name: Empirical broad-spectrum with a susceptibility result — de-escalate
rules.message: A culture and susceptibility result is available — de-escalate empirical broad-spectrum therapy to culture-directed treatment.
rules.explanation: Empirical broad-spectrum cover is a bridge until the organism and its susceptibilities are known. Once a susceptibility result is available, continuing the broad agent needlessly selects for resistance. WHO stewardship prompts de-escalation to the narrowest effective agent the result supports.
rules.requiredAction: Review the susceptibility result and de-escalate to the narrowest effective agent it supports; if broad cover is still required, record why.
sourceRefs: WHO AWaRe / AMS toolkit 2019 — de-escalation to culture-directed therapy

adaptation.whoStatement: De-escalate empirical broad-spectrum therapy to culture-directed treatment once susceptibility results are available.

testCases.name: broad-spectrum with a result available — prompt de-escalation
broad-spectrum but no result yet — do not prompt
not on empirical broad-spectrum — rule does not apply
susceptibility availability never recorded — cannot conclude

rules.name: WHO AWaRe Reserve antibiotic started without stewardship approval
rules.message: A WHO AWaRe Reserve antibiotic has been started without stewardship approval — obtain approval or review the choice.
rules.explanation: Reserve-group agents in the WHO AWaRe classification are last-resort antibiotics whose use must be preserved for confirmed or suspected multidrug-resistant infection. WHO stewardship restricts them to prescriptions approved by an antimicrobial stewardship team so that they are not eroded by routine use.
rules.requiredAction: Obtain antimicrobial stewardship team approval for the Reserve agent, or switch to an appropriate Access- or Watch-group alternative; record the approval or the review decision.
sourceRefs: WHO AWaRe antibiotic classification 2019 — Reserve group restriction; WHO AMS toolkit 2019 — pre-authorisation

adaptation.whoStatement: WHO AWaRe Reserve-group antibiotics should be used only when approved, and reserved for confirmed or suspected multidrug-resistant infection.

testCases.name: Reserve agent started, no approval — block for approval
Reserve agent started with approval — permitted
no Reserve agent started — rule does not apply
approval status never recorded — cannot conclude unapproved

rules.name: Antibiotic started without a documented indication or stop/review date
rules.message: Antibiotic started without a documented indication and/or stop/review date — record both.
rules.explanation: WHO stewardship requires that every antibiotic prescription carry a documented indication and a stop or review date, so the next clinician knows why it was started and when to reassess. A missing indication or stop/review date is the commonest reason a course is silently continued past its purpose.
rules.requiredAction: Record the indication and a stop or review date for the prescription; where either is genuinely not yet determinable, record why and set an early review.
sourceRefs: WHO AWaRe / AMS toolkit 2019 — document indication and stop/review date

adaptation.whoStatement: Every antibiotic prescription should have a documented indication and a stop or review date.
evidenceRefs: WHO AWaRe / AMS toolkit 2019 — prescription documentation

testCases.name: indication not documented — prompt documentation
stop/review date not documented — prompt documentation
both documented — nothing to prompt
no antibiotic started at this contact — rule does not apply
whether an antibiotic was started never recorded — cannot conclude

rules.name: WHO AWaRe Watch antibiotic continued past the review point
rules.message: A WHO AWaRe Watch antibiotic has continued past the review point — review the need to continue, narrow or stop.
rules.explanation: Watch-group agents in the WHO AWaRe classification have higher resistance potential and are prioritised as stewardship targets. Continuing a Watch-group antibiotic beyond a few days without review is a common driver of avoidable resistance; WHO stewardship prompts an early, active review of continuation.
rules.requiredAction: Review the Watch-group antibiotic: confirm the indication still holds, de-escalate to an Access-group agent where the susceptibility allows, and record the decision to continue, narrow or stop.
sourceRefs: WHO AWaRe antibiotic classification 2019 — Watch group as stewardship target; WHO AMS toolkit 2019 — review

adaptation.whoStatement: WHO AWaRe Watch-group antibiotics are priority stewardship targets and their continuation should be actively reviewed.
adaptation.nationalStatement: The review point for Watch-group continuation is provisionally set at 5 days pending the national antimicrobial guideline; the principle of prioritised Watch-group review is adopted as published.
adaptation.rationale: WHO designates the Watch group as a stewardship priority but does not set a universal day cut-off. The 5-day threshold is an engineering placeholder to trigger review earlier than the general course review, and must be replaced by indication-specific durations on national ratification.

testCases.name: Watch agent continued past review point — prompt review
Watch agent still within early window — do not prompt
no Watch agent started — rule does not apply
duration never recorded — cannot conclude past review point
